style: Say calmly and curiously, like a librarian helping you check a surprising fact
lines: Set the sliders, then press Test everyone.
Drag Predict to your guess, then press Lock in guess.
Press Positives only to look at just the people who tested positive.
Tap a row or a column to divide by it. Then drag each question onto its fraction.
Everyone who tested positive takes the test again. Follow the branches, or tap Chances to see probabilities.
Tap a case card, drag Predict to your answer, then press Show answer.
Most of these positives are false alarms. The healthy crowd is just so much bigger.
Close. Your guess is near the calculated share.
The test knows nothing, so a positive tells you nothing new.
Change How common to compare another town, or open Table to inspect the denominator.
Compare your prediction with the result, then tap another case card.
Select a question, then tap its fraction. You can also drag a question onto a fraction.
That is a different group to divide by. Try the fraction shown in the hint.
That fraction matches the question. Select another question to compare denominators.
Tap a glossary term, then press Close glossary to return.
Select a question first, then tap or drag it onto a fraction.
Read the pooled share in the chart. Press New run to try another seed.
Catches: among people who have it, the share who test positive. Tap another term, or press Close glossary.
Clears: among people who do not have it, the share who test negative. Tap another term, or press Close glossary.
How common: the share of the whole town who have it. Tap another term, or press Close glossary.
A person who is well but tests positive. Tap another term, or press Close glossary.
A person who has it but tests negative. Tap another term, or press Close glossary.
This is the worked example from the hint. Compare its two groups, then select another question.
